text:
alex: Heads up — seeing a sharp spike in queued inference requests from hosted clusters in us-west1. Correlates with multiple spot GPU nodegroup deletions happening in the same ~10s window.
alex: Pods are getting SIGTERM almost simultaneously; proxy retry fanout is causing 502/504 bursts and transient throttles.
alex: Quick repro log snippet:
```bash
kubectl get pods -A | grep -E 'Terminating|Evicted' | wc -l
# output: 120
kubectl describe node gtx-spot-xx | grep -i 'shutdown\|eviction'
``` 
alex: Proposal: coalesce node termination handling and increase drain/grace windows for spot GPU pools. Specifically:
- Add a small coalescing daemonset that delays SIGTERM handling for runtime containers so drain events from a single AZ don't create a simultaneous bulk termination.
- Temporarily increase CA scale-down tuning for spot nodegroups (scale-down-unneeded-time 5m -> 12m, and add jitter on deletion)
- Tighten PodDisruptionBudgets for core runtime pods (minAvailable ~80%)
marie: Can we instead jitter the actual node deletions? e.g. random 0-30s delay before kubelet delete. That keeps pods from clustering their SIGTERMs.
samir: Oncall alert shows ~6k 502s between 11:02-11:08, p95 latency jumped ~320ms. PDBs would help, but they also increase steady-state replica count -> cost.
jen: We have PDBs but they are global. Would be nice to make them per-az / per-nodepool topologySpread so evictions don't coincide.
alex: I'll prototype a small coalescing handler as a DaemonSet that traps SIGTERM, checks for nearby node deletions via metadata, and waits up to 90s for the kube drain wave to finish. PR will be small.
oncall-bot: Alert: gpu-nodegroup-scale-down-spiral triggered (us-west1). 502-rate high. Incident channel: #incidents
marie: Also saw that kube-controller churned node objects when spot prices spiked which caused multiple nodegroups to scale down together. Suggest: add a safety window and grouping key (nodepool+az) to CA deletion logic.
samir: Another mitigation: raise reserved capacity buffer on critical pools by +5% during peak hours so eviction waves hit fewer production pods. Cost impact estimate: ~$2.5k/mo for the change, probably acceptable vs customer impact.
jen: SGTM. We should canary the daemonset on eng-infra-canary nodepool first and measure p95 + queued request counts.
alex: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pulls/512 — daemonset implements SIGTERM coalescing and watches node termination API. :thumbsup:
marie: Deployed to canary at 11:40. Early numbers: queued inference requests std dev down ~60% over 15m, p95 latency back to baseline. :eyes:
samir: Nice. Next: run a chaos preemptible wave (100 node spot-evict) and validate no large proxy spike. If good, roll to all us-west1 spot pools.
jen: I'll schedule chaos for 14:00 UTC and invite eng-runtime + infra.
alex: Plan to also relax scale-down aggression: set --scale-down-unneeded-time=12m, --scale-down-delay-after-add=10m on CA for spot pools and enable deletion jitter script starting 02:00 UTC tomorrow.
marie: Estimated cost delta: ~5% more running hours on spot pools during peak -> ~$2.2k/mo. Approve.
samir: We should add an automated regression test in our chaos suite to catch this class of wave-based terminations.
jen: Adding to backlog and will pilot the test after chaos run.
alex: OK rolling the changes to canary now, will promote to prod if chaos run looks good. Will follow up with short postmortem if we still see residual blips. :rocket:
